page: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core with 2 threads. The processor operates at a base frequency of 4.2 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations.

This server is configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, representing a low-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. For local storage, it includes a 118 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2108.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1941.19. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is limited; the stress-ng multi-core score is 1984.89, and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is poor at 21.01 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance fall into the lower performance tiers.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D2lds_v6 offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or complex rendering workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads), 4.0 GB of RAM, and a 118 GB local disk. The CPU supports advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX). Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2108.0 and high single-threaded gzip compression. However, its low memory capacity and weak multi-core scaling limit its performance in memory-intensive tasks, as reflected in its lower memory bandwidth and database operation scores. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, compute-focused workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale text generation, rather than memory-heavy databases or parallelized compilation.
